2. Perused the record.

3. Instant application for bail has been filed by applicant-Priyanka Yadav seeking her enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 575 of 2022 under Sections 498A, 306 I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 D. P. Act,
Police Station-Jeeyanpur, District-Azamgarh, during the pendency of trial.

4. At the very outset, the learned counsel for applicant submits that Suryamani Yadav @ Guddu, the husband of the deceased has already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide order dated Priyanka Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58120526/

For ready reference, the order dated 04.07.2023 is reproduced herein-under:
"

1. Heard Mr. Sunil Kumar, Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Raj Kishore Mishra, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mr. Prem Prakash Yadav, the learned counsel representing first informant.
2. Perused the record.
3.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant-Suryamani Yadav @ Guddu seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 575 of 2022, under Sections 498A,
306 IPC and Sections 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Jiyanpur,
District-Azamgarh during the pendency of trial.
4. Record shows that marriage of applicant was solemnized with Smt. Rekha Yadav (deceased) on 06.06.2010.

However, after expiry of a period of more than 12 years from the date of marriage of applicant, an unfortunate incident occurred on 14.09.2020, in which, the wife of applicant committed suicide by hanging herself.
The information with regard to the aforesaid occurrence at the police station was not given by applicant or any of his family members but by the father of the deceased namely Omprakash Yadav.

Therefore, an FIR dated 15.09.2022 was lodged by first informant-Omprakash Yadav which was registered as Case Crime No. 575 of 2022,
under Sections 498A, 306 IPC and Sections 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Jiyanpur, District-Azamgarh.

In the aforesaid FIR, 5 persons namely - (1)
Suryamani Yadav (Husband), (2) Sheshmani Yadav (Devar), (3) Priyanka Yadav (Devrani) (4) Chandramuni Yadav (Mother-in-law) and (5) Anupama Yadav (Nanad)
have been nominated as named accused.
5. The gravamen of the allegations made in the FIR is to the effect that the marriage of the daughter of the first informant was solemnized with applicant-Suryamani Yadav @ Guddu on 06.06.2010.
At the time of marriage, sufficient amount of goods and dowry was given.
However, the Son-in-law of first informant i.e. applicant and his family members were not satisfied with the same.
Consequently, demand of additional dowry was made.
However, as demand of additional dowry was not satisfied, therefore, physical and mental cruelty was committed upon the daughter of the first informant.
Ultimately, the daughter of the first informant is reported to have been killed by named accused on 14.09.2022.

6. At the very outset, Mr. Sunil Kumar, Advocate appearing on behalf of applicant contends that the bail application of Chandramuni Yadav (Mother of the applicant)
has been rejected by this Court vide order dated 21.12.2022 passed in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 47292 of 2022 (Chandramuni Yadav Vs. State of U.P.).

sentences.text:
This bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant, Chandramuni Yadav,
seeking bail in Case Crime No. 575 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 306 IPC and 3/4 DP Act, Police Station Jeeyanpur, District Azamgarh.

The contention of the learned counsel for the applicant is that the present bail application is filed by mother-in-law, the husband of the deceased was suffering from cancer and troubled by this fact the deceased committed suicide.
In any case the death was beyond seven years of marriage.

Learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant has drawn attention of the court to the post mortem report which states that ligature mark found during post mortem runs all around the neck and, therefore, it is contended that it has not been a case of suicide.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and after perusing the averments made in the present bail application as well as rejection order, this Court is of the considered opinion, that no case for grant of bail to the applicant is made out.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected."

7. It is next contended that the bail application of Sheshmani Yadav (Devar of the deceased) has been allowed by this Court vide order dated 13.02.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 1937 of 2023 (Sheshmani Yadav Vs. State of U.P.).

"1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A for the State and perused the record.
2.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Learned counsel further submits that the applicant is a Dewar of the deceased, who was living separately from the deceased and her husband.

He further submits that the is no evidence on record to demonstrate that the applicant has abetted the deceased to commit suicide and therefore no offence under Section 306 I.P.C. is made out against the applicant.

Learned counsel has submitted that since the applicant was living separately from the deceased, therefore there was question for demand of dowry and that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case merely on the ground that he is a dewar of the deceased.
Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the applicant have also been placed before the Court.
The circumstances which, according to the counsel, led to the false implication of the accused have also been mentioned.

It has also been assured on behalf of the applicant Priyanka Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58120526/
3 that he is ready to cooperate with the process of law and shall faithfully make himself available before the court whenever required and is also ready to accept all the conditions which the Court may deem fit to impose upon him.

sentences.text: He next submits that applicant is languishing in jail since 30.11.2022 having no criminal history.

3. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the innocence of the applicant cannot be adjudged at pre trial stage,
therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence.
In case the applicant is released on bail he will again indulge in similar activities and will misuse the liberty of bail.

4. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of evidence, and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
Hence the bail application is allowed.

5. Let applicant Sheshmani Yadav, involved in Case Crime No.575 of 2022 under Sections 498A, 306 I.P.C., and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Jeeyanpur, District Azamgarh, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
A. The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
B. The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
C. The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
D. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is an accused, or suspected, of the commission of he is suspected.
E. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the trial Court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of the applicant in accordance with law."

After arguing for some time, applicant's counsel submits that the present application for anticipatory bail may be dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file a regular bail application which may be decided keeping in view the guidelines as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.

In view of the above, considering the aforesaid alternative prayer made by learned counsel for the applicant, it is directed that the applicant shall surrender before the concerned court below within four weeks from today and in case a regular bail application is filed, the same be decided in view of the law laid by Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra).
For the period of four weeks from today or till the time of surrender of the applicant before the concerned court below, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant- Suryamani Yadav @ Guddu in the above case.
With the above observations and directions, this application is disposed of."

Mr. Sunil Kumar, Advocate appearing on behalf of applicant contends that as per the opinion of the Autopsy Surgeon, the cause of death of the deceased is Asphyxia as a result of anti-mortem hanging.
He, therefore, contends that the issue as to whether the death of the deceased is suicidal or homicidal is subject to trial evidence.

However, up to this stage, none of the ingredients of Section 107 IPC are satisfied against applicant inasmuch as there is nothing to indicate abetment,
instigation or conspiracy against applicant.

Applicant is in jail since 20.12.2022.
As such, he has undergone more than 6 months of incarceration.

The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted,
therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant now stands crystallized.
However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the course of trial.

11. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. and Mr. Prem Prakash Yadav, the learned counsel representing first informant have opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The present case is a case of homicidal death and not suicidal.
The Autopsy Surgeon has clearly recorded that ligature mark was found all around the neck of the deceased, which itself goes to show that present case is not a case of hanging but strangulation.
As such, applicant does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.

12. In rejoinder, Mr. Sunil Kumar, Advocate appearing on behalf of applicant has invited the attention of Court to the order of this Court dated 14.06.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 22216 of 2023 (Gulab Yadav and 2 Others Vs. State of U.P.).

sentences.text: Subsequent to above, the postmortem of the body of the deceased was conducted.
The doctor who conducted the autopsy of the body of the decease opined that the cause of death of deceased was Asphyxia as a result of ante mortem hanging.

Autopsy surgeon found following ante mortem injuries on the body of the deceased- "Ligature mark- size 4cm x 1cm, all around neck 6cm below from Left Ear lowbule and 4 cm below from Right Ear lowbule, below Chin, above Thyroid.
Ligature Mark- oblique, base- groove brownish and parchment like.
or cut sub contusion, hard, white & glistening.

Except for ligature mark, the autopsy surgeon did not find any other external or internal injury on the body of the deceased."
6.

After expiry of a period of five days from the date of occurrence i.e. 28.02.2023, a delayed F.I.R.
dated 05.03.2023 was lodged by the first informant namely Smt Razia, widow of the deceased and was registered as Case Crime No. 75 of 2023 under Section 302 I.P.C. P.S.- Maharajganj, District- Azamgarh.
In the aforesaid F.I.R. three persons namely Pappu Yadav, Gulab Yadav and Balwant Yadav have been nominated as named accused.

7. After completion of investigation, Investigating Officer submitted the charge sheet dated 02.06.2023 whereby all the named accused have been charge sheeted under Section 306 I.P.C.
8.Learned
counsel for applicants contends that applicants are innocent.
They have been falsely implicated in above named case crime number.
The present case is a case of circumstantial evidence and therefore, there is no eyewitness of the occurrence.

According to the learned counsel for applicant, the guilt of an accused in a crime based upon circumstantial evidence can be inferred only if the golden test laid down by the Apex Court in Sharad Birdhichand Sarda Vs. State of Maharashtra 1984 AIR 1622 (Pg- 152) is satisfied against the accused.

It is further contended that no strong motive has emerged against the applicant for committing the crime in question.
According to learned counsel for applicants, as per the medical opinion, the present case is a case of suicidal death.

However, with reference to Section 107 of the Evidence Act, the learned counsel for applicants submits that up to this stage, no such material has emerged on the basis of which conspiracy, abetment or instigation can be inferred against the applicant for committing the crime in question.
Reference has also been made the following four judgments - (i).

Sarvesh Vs. State of U.P. 2018 ADJ Online 0163.

sentences.text: On basis of above, learned counsel for applicants contends that no such circumstance has emerged during the course of investigation which may lead to the inference that deceased had committed suicide on account of an immediate act of applicant.
Even otherwise, applicants 2 and 3 are men of clean antecedents in as much as they have no criminal history to their credit except the present one.
Applicant 1, Gulab Yadav has criminal history of two cases, which has been sufficiently explained.
The charge sheet having been submitted, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon the prosecution against applicants, now stands crystalized.
No such circumstance has emerged during the course of investigation on the basis of which it can be urged that custodial arrest of applicants is absolutely necessary during the course of trial.
On the above premise, the learned counsel for applicants submits that applicants are liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, applicants are enlarged on bail, they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with the trial.
10. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. and Mr. Madhavanand Shukla, the learned counsel representing first informant have opposed the prayer for bail.
The learned counsel representing the first informant has disputed the medical evidence by referring to the post mortem report.
He contends that the present case is a case of strangulation and not a suicidal death.
However, he could not establish the submission urged by him with reference to the material on record.
11. Learned A.G.A. also could not dislodge the submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicants with reference to the record at this stage.

12. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicants, the learned A.G.A. for State, the learned counsel for first informant and upon perusal of record, evidence, acquisitions made and complicity of applicants coupled with the fact that death of the deceased is a suicidal death, there being nothing on record to show that the deceased had committed suicide on account of an immediate act of applicants, present case is a case of circumstantial evidence, the golden test laid down by the Supreme Court in Sharad Birdhichand Sarda(supra) does not satisfied against the applicants up to this stage, the clean antecedents of applicants 2 and 3, the criminal history of applicant 1, having been explained sufficiently, the charge sheet having been submitted, but no such circumstance has emerged during the course of investigation necessitating the custodial arrest of applicants, the judgment of the Supreme Court in S. Subhashchandra Gangwal Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 373 (Paragraph 5), but without making any comments on the merits of the case, the applicants have made out a case for bail.

the credibility or the reliability of the medical evidence can be contradicted only during the course of trial, no such circumstance has been pointed out by the learned A.G.A. or the learned counsel for first informant that the deceased committed suicide on account of an immediate act of the applicant, the provisions contained in Section 107 read with Section 306 IPC.

Prima-facie there is nothing to indicate abetment,
instigation or conspiracy against applicant, the judgments of Supreme Court referred to above, the clean antecedents of applicant, but without making any comments on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.
14. The bail application is accordingly allowed.
